note: The ZEK, the Zurich-based association that keeps Switzerland's register of credit information, says on its own 'About us' page (read 2026-10-31) that it works over the whole of Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein; Liechtenstein is written from the ZEK's rules as Switzerland's file is (CH.json), and in the same readings. The ZEK's Reglement I (version V1.04-05-2026), s.3.9: members report the credit data on payment arrears at once, at the latest within a month: written as reported 30 days after the due date. Its list of retention periods (V1.2020-25-10): a card blocked by its issuer stays five years from the negative event (two years from the block's lifting, the first to end deleting it); a reported contract with a partial or total loss five years from the credit-status date: written as keep 5, with no clears, as Switzerland's file has it. No Liechtenstein law or regulator's text on credit bureaus was read (gesetze.li's search gives curl no results; llv.li answered with a Cloudflare check); the Swiss IKO is a Swiss federal body under the Swiss Consumer Credit Act and isn't named for Liechtenstein.

sources.title: ZEK: Über uns
sources.said: Die ZEK übt ihre Tätigkeit über das Gebiet der ganzen Schweiz und des Fürstentum Liechtenstein aus.

sources.title: ZEK, Reglement I (V1.04-05-2026)
